Your first job is about learning how to contribute, not proving you already know everything.

- Ask questions early, but first take a little time to investigate. Share what you tried and where you got stuck.
- Make small, focused changes. They’re easier to review, test, and understand.
- Read existing code and tests to learn the team’s conventions before introducing new patterns.
- Communicate progress and blockers. A timely “I need help” is more useful than a surprise missed deadline.
- Treat code review as collaboration, not a judgment of your ability.
- Keep notes on setup steps, unfamiliar concepts, and useful commands.
- Build sustainable habits. You don’t need to work every evening to become a good engineer.

### 3
Sunlight looks white, but it’s actually a mixture of colors. When it enters Earth’s atmosphere, it hits tiny air molecules that scatter some of the light in different directions.

Blue light gets scattered much more than red light, so blue light reaches your eyes from all across the sky—not just straight from the Sun. That’s why the sky looks blue!

You might wonder why it isn’t violet, which scatters even more. Sunlight contains less violet, and our eyes are less sensitive to it, so we see the sky as blue.
